pages.title: Diesel dominates net imports, and fuel sales concentrate in Gauteng, KZN and Western Cape
pages.layout: Retain native PowerPoint table: Agenda / SCR / Finding / Implication for Vopak / Supporting pages. Retain existing shapes for SCR labels. Update links after final ordering.
rows: Market baseline
S1
Diesel accounts for most net imports. In 2024, net diesel imports were 9.997 bn litres, compared with 3.081 bn litres for petrol.
Diesel import flows are the largest observed trade component to assess against Vopak's services.
S2
Gauteng, KZN and Western Cape account for 68.6% of reported 2022 petrol and diesel sales.
Gauteng and KZN are the first demand markets to assess against Lesedi and Durban.
Market changes
C3
OCGT generation has fallen sharply since FY2024. Freight activity and changing vehicle sales affect other parts of fuel demand.
Forecast each end use separately. A single growth rate would miss changes in the demand mix.
C4
Published refining capacity fell from 718 to 358 thousand barrels/day between 2020 and 2022. Future plant output remains uncertain.
Domestic production assumptions materially affect the forecast import requirement.
C5
Matola and Walvis Bay provide alternative fuel supply nodes. Their effect on inland competition still needs route and volume evidence.
Compare competing supply routes to the same inland market.
Vopak outlook
R6
Vopak has facilities in Durban and Lesedi, alongside the coastal and inland markets identified in the demand analysis.
Establish current fuel volumes and usable capacity at these sites before estimating additional business.
R7
The evidence does not yet establish a need for additional storage. Customer volumes and usable spare capacity remain unverified.
Determine how much additional fuel existing assets could handle, then assess any remaining capacity requirement.

sections: Imports of 10.793 bn litres less exports of 0.796 bn litres give net imports of 9.997 bn litres.
Imports of 4.001 bn litres less exports of 0.920 bn litres give net imports of 3.081 bn litres.
Reported sales and model estimates remain separate. The workbook reconciles each product and identifies the missing coverage.

pages.speaker_note: The former 20.763 bn litre figure sums selected 2024 reported petrol and diesel sales. It is not a model demand result. The recorded workbook has 16.433 bn litres of road petrol/diesel demand and 23.984 bn litres when the additional modelled diesel sectors are included. The broader diesel scope includes marine and remains unreconciled. Neither total is presented as a verified replacement market size.

pages.title: C5. Matola and Walvis Bay add alternative supply nodes to the inland market
pages.layout: Retain the editable regional map. Label gateway origins and the common Gauteng destination clearly. Right-hand text shapes distinguish existing alternatives, proposed inland nodes and evidence of market change.
sections: The published inventory includes 60,000 m3 of petrol/diesel storage at Matola's GIMTL and 65,000 m3 at Walvis Bay's NOSF.
The Transnet depot lease offers identify possible inland distribution nodes. Refurbishment, licensing and commercial operation remain conditional.
What would demonstrate a market shift
Commissioning dates, growth in handled volumes and changes in delivered cost would show whether these nodes are changing inland supply patterns.

rows: Durban
KZN accounts for 19.6% of reported 2022 fuel sales. Diesel is the largest component of national net imports.
Assess coastal demand and inland flows that Durban could handle.
Current product volumes, customer destinations and usable fuel capacity.
Lesedi
Gauteng accounts for 31.1% of reported 2022 fuel sales, the largest provincial share.
Assess inland demand against Lesedi's receipt and dispatch capability.
Current throughput and the full delivered cost from competing gateways.
Competing nodes
Matola and Walvis Bay have published petrol/diesel storage. Inland depot lease offers could add distribution points.
Establish where alternative supply routes could change Vopak's inland business.
Operating status, handled volumes, route costs and service to the same destinations.
pages.closing_copy: The current evidence identifies priority markets. It does not yet quantify additional Vopak volumes or a requirement for new tanks.
